title: Commit the payment before sending the notification
dek: Moving publication past the commit prevents notifications for rolled-back payments, but leaves delivery as a separate operation.
meta: Fictional component study · Source and in-memory probe results
footer: Based on the supplied source and probes. No real database or process-kill simulation was performed.

sections.title: Two operations, one transaction boundary
sections.content: Lantern Ledger marks a payment as paid and publishes a notification. Previously, both calls ran inside the database transaction callback. The database commits staged writes only after that callback fulfills. Publication, however, is external: placing it inside the callback does not make the notification part of the database transaction.

sections.title: A notification could outlive a rollback
sections.content: If publication succeeded and the commit then failed, the payment rolled back while its notification remained visible. The supplied probe records exactly that outcome: an unpaid record and one notification. A publication error after external delivery could produce the same mismatch, because rejecting the callback rolled back only the database writes.

sections.title: Wait for the commit, then publish
sections.content:
The changed function first awaits the transaction:

{{CODE:0}}

That await completes after commit, not merely after markPaid. A write or commit rejection exits the function before publication. In the supplied in-memory results, a failed commit now leaves zero notifications.

Publication follows outside the callback:

{{CODE:1}}

A publication rejection still rejects the function, but cannot undo the committed payment. The probes show both possibilities: rejection before delivery leaves zero notifications; rejection after delivery leaves one. The author describes payment and notification as atomic, but this code establishes ordering, not an all-or-nothing result.

sections.title: A stronger order, not guaranteed delivery
sections.content: Failed payment transactions no longer trigger publication. A process stop between commit and publication can still leave a paid record without a notification; no durable outbox or background retry is supplied. Retrying after uncertain delivery can duplicate notifications. Idempotent markPaid protects the payment write, not delivery: both versions produce two notifications under concurrent calls in the probe. These results support the ordering change, not exactly-once delivery or atomicity.
